Read one time step's full depth column, keeping the deepest wet level

Source: R/copernicus.R
read_day_deepest.Rd

The reanalysis publishes temperature at the sea floor but not salinity, so a sea-floor salinity has to be taken from the three-dimensional field: fetch the whole column and keep, in each cell, the deepest level that holds a value.

Usage

read_day_deepest(item, code, name)

Arguments

item

one work item, as built by accessCopernicus()

code

the Copernicus code fetched, e.g. so

name

what to call the result column, e.g. BOTS

Value

a data frame with the value, the depth it came from, YEAR, MONTH and DAY

What "deepest wet level" means

A model cell is NA below the sea floor, so the last level carrying a value is the bottom-most one the model resolves there. That is the same convention Copernicus's own bottomT follows, which is why the two pair.

It is not the sea floor itself. Level spacing coarsens with depth — from a metre near the surface to several hundred at abyssal depths — so in deep water the value can sit a long way above the real bottom. The depth actually used is returned alongside the value rather than left to be assumed, in a <name>_depth column.
